Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back.
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

India’s real challenge starts now, as they step up to chase on a surface that’s showing considerably more turn today than on the first two days. Only once has a target of over 300 been chased successfully in India during the fourth innings, and that was back in 2008, when the home side accomplished the feat against England. This statistic underscores the monumental challenge that awaits India here. Even with ample time on their side, the deteriorating pitch conditions will only make the task harder as the match progresses. Back in a bit for India's reply.

New Zealand lose their last 5 wickets for just 57 runs this morning to be bowled out for 255, setting India a target of 359 runs. The day began brightly, with runs flowing smoothly as Glenn Phillips and Tom Blundell resumed their partnership. However, Blundell's dismissal triggered a rapid collapse, turning what seemed a comfortable start into a parade of wickets. India would have aimed to wrap up the New Zealand innings within an hour, and they’ve succeeded. Ravindra Jadeja, after a quiet Test up to this point, made a vital impact, accounting for 3 of the final 5 wickets to fall.

OUT! RUN OUT! It's all over and New Zealand are dismissed for 255 runs in the first hour of the day. Brilliant presence of mind from Jadeja. Jadeja drops it short outside off and Glenn Phillips slaps the ball to the right of Washington Sundar at sweeper covers and sets off for a couple of runs. Washington Sundar is a bit slow on the ball but picks it up at once and fires in a throw at Ravindra Jadeja standing at the bowler's end. Jadeja gets the throw on the bounce and he flicks it towards the stumps beside him. The ball hits the bails and it looks like William O'Rourke is struggling. The decision is sent upstairs and William O'Rourke is found short of his ground with his bat still on the crease. New Zealand are all out for 255 runs and they stand on a lead of 358 runs.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull is near the deck. He says that it is a gorgeous morning here in Pune as history beckons for New Zealand. Dinesh Karthik joins him and says that it is going to turn a lot more than it did in the first two days. He observes that the cracks have widened slightly and the surface looks increasingly abrasive. Karthik praises New Zealand's proactive approach against the spinners, highlighting how they disrupted the bowlers' lengths with effective sweep shots and by stepping down the track. He suggests that India may need to adopt a similar strategy to counter the Kiwi spin threat and stay in the game.

Whenever it is their turn to bat, India will look to their seasoned batters like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma to step up, while New Zealand will aim to continue applying pressure with a disciplined bowling approach. So, sit tight and enjoy every ball, as Day 3 promises to deliver another captivating chapter in this thrilling Test match.

As for New Zealand, when they were bowled out for 259 in the first innings, it felt that they left a few runs out there, considering the position they were in at one point.
